questions.question: What is the main raw material used to produce traditional plastic food packaging?
options: Fossil fuels
Wood pulp
Plant starches
Recycled glass

questions.question: Why does plastic waste in landfills and oceans pose a major environmental threat to organisms?
options: It dissolves quickly and increases water acidity
It degrades very slowly and can cause physical harm to wildlife
It absorbs solar radiation and cools the local climate
It acts as a fertilizer, causing rapid plant overgrowth

questions.question: Which of the following is considered a sustainable alternative to traditional plastic packaging?
options: Chlorinated PVC films
Biodegradable bioplastics made from renewable resources
Non-recyclable polystyrene containers
Heavy metal-infused synthetic wraps

questions.question: What is a primary environmental benefit of using plastic packaging for food items?
options: It increases the nutritional value of the food
It prevents food spoilage and reduces food waste
It absorbs carbon dioxide from the surrounding air
It speeds up the natural decomposition of food

questions.question: When deciding whether to use plastic food packaging, what must we carefully weigh the benefits against?
options: The decrease in transport costs and storage space
The production emissions and damage to biodiversity
The taste improvements and color preservation of food
The increase in the geological age of Earth's crust

questions.question: What is one of the major driving forces behind global deforestation?
options: Converting natural forested land for agricultural use
Building offshore wind farms in coastal areas
Developing underground transport networks
Creating conservation reserves for endangered birds

questions.question: How does deforestation directly affect many forest-dwelling species?
options: It increases their hunting efficiency by clearing trees
It leads to severe habitat loss
It forces them to hibernate during the summer months
It speeds up their reproductive cycles

questions.question: Which mitigation strategy helps restore damaged ecosystems and combat biodiversity loss?
options: Expanding industrial monoculture farming
Reforestation and rewilding projects
Increasing the use of synthetic chemical fertilizers
Clearing older forests to make space for fast-growing crops

questions.question: Why is global food production currently considered to be at risk?
options: Due to global warming and climate change
Due to a sudden increase in atmospheric oxygen levels
Due to the replacement of agricultural land with natural forests
Due to a worldwide decline in the demand for food

questions.question: How do extreme weather events, made more common by climate change, impact food production?
options: They make it much more challenging to grow and harvest crops
They guarantee stable and predictable crop yields every year
They eliminate the need for agricultural irrigation systems
They increase the global surface area of fertile soil

questions.question: How can making conscious changes to our daily diets help protect the environment?
options: By reducing greenhouse gas emissions from food production
By encouraging the use of non-recyclable packaging
By increasing the demand for imported fossil fuels
By speeding up the rate of global deforestation

questions.question: Why does deforestation disrupt the global carbon cycle?
options: It increases the rate of mineral weathering in soil
Less carbon dioxide is absorbed from the atmosphere for photosynthesis
It stops animals from releasing carbon dioxide during respiration
It completely prevents carbon from dissolving in ocean waters

questions.question: What role does carbon dioxide (CO2) play in global climate change?
options: It acts as a greenhouse gas that enhances the greenhouse effect
It reflects all incoming solar radiation back into deep space
It destroys the ozone layer to allow more cooling of the Earth
It condenses in the atmosphere to form highly alkaline rain

questions.question: How does deforestation disrupt the water cycle?
options: By increasing the total volume of water on Earth
Because less water is absorbed and transpired by trees
By stopping all evaporation from lakes and oceans
Because it accelerates the formation of glaciers

questions.question: How does climate change affect species that are highly adapted to their specific habitats?
options: It alters habitat conditions, making species less well adapted to live there
It immediately grants them new genetic mutations to thrive in any climate
It protects them from competing with non-native species
It stabilizes the local temperatures to prevent migration
